title: A multicentre, prospective observational phase IV clinical study to assess the impact of lebrikizumab on burdensome body areas in patients with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis – the ADimpact study
summary: The ADimpact study will collect information on the effectiveness and safety of treatment with Ebglyss® (lebrikizumab) in adolescents and adults with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis who are receiving treatment in routine clinical practice. The study will also examine patients' experiences with the disease and its treatment, including the effects on itching, sleep, quality of life, daily activities, and overall disease burden. Particular attention will be paid to areas of the body that are often especially troublesome for patients, such as the face, hands, feet, scalp, neck, genital area, and nails.

interventions.name: To evaluate the impact of lebrikizumab on dermatology-related quality of life, as measured by the DLQI in the adult population and by cDLQI in the adolescent population, in patients with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis treated under real-world conditions over 52 weeks.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adolescent (>12 to <18 years and weighing ≥40 kg, where applicable) and adult (>18 years) patients with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis and involvement of at least one burdensome body area (scalp, face, neck, hands, feet, genitalia, or nails), who are either naïve to advanced systemic therapy for atopic dermatitis or have previously received no more than one advanced systemic therapy that was discontinued prior to study enrolment, and who are prescribed lebrikizumab (Ebglyss®) according to the SmPC in routine clinical practice.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients not eligible for treatment with Ebglyss® (lebrikizumab) according to the approved SmPC, patients with prior exposure to lebrikizumab or more than one prior advanced systemic therapy for atopic dermatitis, and patients participating in another clinical trial at baseline or during the planned study period.
